stem: What is the expected natural history and prognosis for a typical case of croup?

options.text: Most children recover within 48 to 72 hours.
Recovery usually takes 10 to 14 days, with a persistent cough for weeks.
Symptoms frequently progress to bacterial tracheitis in over $50\%$ of cases.
Once recovered, children are immune to further episodes of croup.

explanation: Croup typically has a short duration, with symptoms of airway swelling resolving relatively quickly compared to lower airway infections.
rationale: Compare the recovery time of upper respiratory swelling to the longer process of clearing lower airway mucus and debris.

optionExplanations.A: Croup typically has a short duration, with symptoms of airway swelling resolving relatively quickly compared to lower airway infections.
optionExplanations.B: This timeline is more characteristic of bronchiolitis, which involves more extensive tissue repair in the lower airways.
optionExplanations.C: Bacterial tracheitis is a rare differential diagnosis and a severe complication, not the standard progression of viral croup.
optionExplanations.D: Croup actually has an increased frequency of recurrence in children who have had a previous episode.
